description: Synthetic held-out semantic cases frozen before the first live run. They characterize recovery and safety; they do not provide a matched host-only efficacy baseline.

cases.goal: Identify why warm requests return stale account data.
cases.initialEvidence: Warm requests return stale account data while cold requests are fresh; the symptom appeared after cache work.

hypotheses.assumption: Warm requests read the affected cache.

hypotheses.statement: The warm path reuses an expired authorization token.
hypotheses.assumption: Warm requests reuse session authorization state.
predicts: Cache bypass remains stale and the token trace differs.
hypotheses.weakenedBy: Fresh authorization still returns stale data.

check.action: Repeat the warm request with cache bypass and trace the authorization token.

expectedOutcomes.observation: Bypass is fresh and authorization is unchanged.
Bypass stays stale and reveals an expired reused token.

cases.alternateCheck: Compare invalidation events with authorization-session traces.
cases.newEvidence: Cache bypass remained stale; the warm trace reused an expired token, and refreshing authorization returned fresh data.

cases.goal: Explain persistent 503 responses after a retry refactor.
cases.initialEvidence: Persistent 503 responses began after retry code changed, and the new client log shows only one visible attempt.

hypotheses.statement: The retry scheduler exits after one attempt.
hypotheses.assumption: Additional attempts would receive a successful response.
predicts: The old client or forced retries succeed.
hypotheses.weakenedBy: Old and forced-retry clients receive the same terminal response.

hypotheses.statement: The upstream account quota is exhausted.
hypotheses.assumption: Every client uses the same exhausted account.
predicts: All clients fail and quota remaining is zero.
hypotheses.weakenedBy: A request with available quota still fails identically.

check.action: Run old and forced-retry clients while recording the upstream quota header.

expectedOutcomes.observation: Old or forced retries succeed with quota available.
All clients fail and quota remaining is zero.

cases.alternateCheck: Trace scheduler attempt counters without changing account state.
cases.newEvidence: The old client and forced retries returned the same 503; the signed upstream header reported quota remaining zero.

cases.goal: Explain a parser stack failure after a parser upgrade.
cases.initialEvidence: A parser stack failure first appeared immediately after the parser package upgrade.

hypotheses.statement: The upgraded parser regressed on this syntax.
hypotheses.assumption: The failing bytes represent supported syntax.
predicts: The same logical input fails after byte normalization.
hypotheses.weakenedBy: Normalized bytes parse under the same parser.

hypotheses.statement: The fixture contains an invalid byte-order marker.
hypotheses.assumption: Normalization removes the marker without changing syntax.
predicts: Normalized bytes parse under the same parser.

check.action: Normalize the exact fixture bytes and parse with the same upgraded parser.

cases.alternateCheck: Bisect parser versions using the unchanged fixture bytes.
cases.newEvidence: Removing the invalid byte-order marker made the exact fixture parse successfully with the same upgraded parser.

cases.initialEvidence: The failure occurs only in parallel runs; serial runs pass, and concurrent traces show overlapping counter writes.

hypotheses.statement: Unsynchronized counter updates create a race.
hypotheses.assumption: The observed overlapping writes target shared state.
predicts: Serializing counter updates removes the failure.
hypotheses.weakenedBy: The failure remains with serialized updates.

hypotheses.statement: A malformed fixture independently causes the failure.
hypotheses.assumption: The same malformed fixture is used in serial and parallel runs.
predicts: The failure remains when counter updates are serialized.
hypotheses.weakenedBy: The unchanged fixture passes after serialization.

check.action: Serialize counter updates while keeping the fixture and workload unchanged.

expectedOutcomes.observation: Serialization does not remove the failure.

cases.alternateCheck: Validate the fixture independently without changing concurrency.
cases.newEvidence: Serializing counter updates removed the failure; the fixture and workload were unchanged.
